criteria_results.title: Identifies uptime gap: Agreement 99.5% vs. SLS 99.95%
criteria_results.reasoning: A-2 and key metrics table state Agreement 99.5% (efforts-based) vs SLS Tier 1 99.95% guaranteed.

criteria_results.title: Explains practical impact of uptime gap in healthcare context
criteria_results.reasoning: Quantifies 216 vs 21.6 minutes/month, 43.8 vs 4.4 hrs/year across 11 hospitals and 47 clinics, and ties outages to patient care.

criteria_results.title: Identifies scheduled maintenance window inflation (8 hrs/week vs. 4 hrs/month)
criteria_results.reasoning: A-4 identifies 8 hrs/week (32-40 hrs/month) excluded maintenance vs SLS cap of 4 hrs/month.

criteria_results.title: Notes that maintenance window can mask actual downtime
criteria_results.reasoning: A-4 and Appendix A.1 show effective availability could be ~94.1% while SLA is reported as met.

criteria_results.title: Identifies Emergency Maintenance exclusion from downtime calculations
criteria_results.reasoning: A-5 identifies blanket exclusion of Emergency Maintenance with non-binding 'reasonable efforts' 2-hour notice vs SLS §3.3 inclusion unless force majeure.

criteria_results.title: Notes risk of reclassifying outages as emergency maintenance
criteria_results.reasoning: A-5 notes Cloudvance could label any outage, including its own defective release, as Emergency Maintenance and report 100% uptime.

criteria_results.title: Identifies service credit trigger misalignment (credits start at 99.5% vs. 99.94%)
criteria_results.reasoning: B-1 notes credits start only below 99.5% so no credit for months between 99.5% and 99.94%, while SLS credits begin at 99.94%.

criteria_results.title: Identifies service credit cap (15%) vs. SLS uncapped requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: B-1 identifies 15% ($85,500) monthly cap vs SLS uncapped 10% per 0.1% shortfall.

criteria_results.title: Identifies sole-and-exclusive-remedy clause for SLA failures
criteria_results.reasoning: B-3 identifies Ex. C §C.5 sole and exclusive remedy vs SLS §4.3 prohibition; B-4 covers chronic failure (3 in rolling 6 months) actual damages.

criteria_results.title: Identifies non-binding nature of incident response times
criteria_results.reasoning: C-2 identifies 'commercially reasonable targets... not binding' language vs SLS §5.4 binding commitments with consequences.

criteria_results.title: Identifies severity classification mismatch (3-tier vs. 4-tier)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-1 identifies three-level Critical/Major/Minor vs SLS four-tier S1-S4 model.

criteria_results.title: Identifies slower response/resolution times with specific time comparisons
criteria_results.reasoning: C-2 gives specific comparisons: S1 response 2 hrs vs 15 min, resolution 8 vs 4 hrs, etc.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing HITECH Act incorporation in BAA
criteria_results.reasoning: D-1 identifies Ex. D cites only HIPAA/45 CFR 160 and 164 with no HITECH incorporation, failing SLS §6.1.

criteria_results.title: Explains significance of HITECH Act omission
criteria_results.reasoning: D-1 explains significance: direct BA liability, sale-of-PHI prohibition, state AG enforcement, penalties, breach notification.

criteria_results.title: Identifies overbroad license grant to Customer Data
criteria_results.reasoning: E-2 quotes §6.2 license to modify/create derivative works for providing and improving services vs SLS §7.1 strictly-necessary limit.

criteria_results.title: Identifies de-identified data use without opt-out
criteria_results.reasoning: E-2 identifies §6.3 de-identified use for product improvement/analytics without consent, no opt-out, vs SLS §6.5 direct benefit and opt-out.

criteria_results.title: Identifies insufficient post-termination data retrieval period (30 vs. 90 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: E-3 identifies 30-day retrieval vs SLS 90-day minimum.

criteria_results.title: Identifies data format gap (commercially standard vs. HL7 FHIR/CSV)
criteria_results.reasoning: E-3 identifies 'commercially standard format' vs SLS HL7 FHIR and CSV.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing transition assistance plan
criteria_results.reasoning: E-4 identifies no transition assistance vs SLS §7.3 12-month TAP at pre-agreed rates.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing prior written consent for subcontractors handling PHI
criteria_results.reasoning: S-1 identifies no prior written consent (post-engagement notice) vs SLS prior consent with objection right, and notes Stratos pre-approved without diligence.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing subcontractor flow-down obligations
criteria_results.reasoning: S-2 identifies 'sufficient to enable' standard and no flow-down of SLAs, audit rights, destruction vs SLS 'at least as protective'.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing data hosting location restrictions
criteria_results.reasoning: S-3 identifies 'any Stratos U.S. data center' with no schedule by city/state, no 90-day notice and consent.

criteria_results.title: Identifies liability cap below SLS minimum ($6.84M vs. higher amount)
criteria_results.reasoning: F-1 identifies $6.84M cap vs SLS $15.48M (24 months total fees), shortfall $8.64M.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing carve-outs from consequential damages exclusion
criteria_results.reasoning: F-2 identifies no carve-outs and lists data breaches, BAA, IP infringement, gross negligence/willful misconduct.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing cyber liability insurance requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: D-6 identifies only 'commercially reasonable insurance' with no minimum vs SLS $10M cyber coverage.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing HITRUST CSF certification requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: D-4 identifies SOC 2 only with no HITRUST CSF as required by SLS §6.3(b).

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing annual penetration testing requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: D-4 identifies no annual penetration testing requirement.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing requirement to deliver penetration testing reports within 30 days
criteria_results.reasoning: D-4 notes SLS requires full pen test report within 30 days and Agreement gives no right to pen test results.

criteria_results.title: Identifies vague encryption standards (industry-standard vs. AES-256/TLS 1.2+)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-3 identifies 'industry-standard encryption' vs AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+.

criteria_results.title: Identifies termination cure period gap (60 days vs. 30 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: G-1 identifies 60-day cure vs SLS 30 days.

criteria_results.title: Identifies convenience termination notice period gap (180 days vs. 90 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: G-2 identifies 180 days' notice vs SLS 90 days.

criteria_results.title: Identifies convenience termination fee gap (remaining fees vs. no fee)
criteria_results.reasoning: G-2 identifies fee equal to unpaid installments for current contract year vs SLS no fee.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing termination right for chronic SLA failure
criteria_results.reasoning: B-4 identifies no chronic failure termination right vs SLS 3+ failures in rolling 6 months, no cure and no fee.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing termination right for PHI data breach
criteria_results.reasoning: G-3 identifies no data-breach termination right vs SLS §10.4 immediate termination with 10-day conditional cure.

criteria_results.title: Identifies audit frequency gap (1/year vs. 2/year)
criteria_results.reasoning: H-1 identifies once per year vs SLS at least 2 audits per year.

criteria_results.title: Identifies audit notice period gap (60 days vs. 30 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: H-1 identifies 60 days' notice vs SLS 30 days' notice.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing physical data center inspection rights
criteria_results.reasoning: H-1 notes no physical inspection vs SLS §11.2 physical inspection of data centers.

criteria_results.title: Identifies audit limitation allowing SOC 2 report substitution for full audit access
criteria_results.reasoning: H-1 identifies §13.2 SOC 2 report substitution satisfying any audit request.

criteria_results.title: Identifies governing law mismatch (Texas vs. North Carolina)
criteria_results.reasoning: I-1 identifies Texas law vs North Carolina.

criteria_results.title: Identifies mandatory arbitration vs. SLS litigation requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: I-2 identifies AAA arbitration in Austin vs Mecklenburg County litigation and no mandatory arbitration over $1M.

criteria_results.title: Uptime gap rated Critical or High
criteria_results.reasoning: A-2 uptime gap rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: Overbroad data license gap rated Critical or High
criteria_results.reasoning: E-2 data license gap rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap shortfall rated Critical or High
criteria_results.reasoning: F-1 liability cap rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: Missing consequential damages carve-outs rated Critical or High
criteria_results.reasoning: F-2 missing carve-outs rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: Missing HITECH incorporation rated Critical or High
criteria_results.reasoning: D-1 HITECH omission rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: At least 75% of gaps include specific redline language or negotiation points
criteria_results.reasoning: Every Part IV finding includes specific recommended redline language and a negotiation position.

criteria_results.title: References specific Agreement sections or exhibit references
criteria_results.reasoning: Findings cite specific sections and exhibits (Ex. C §C.1, §10.2, Ex. D §D.1, etc.).

criteria_results.title: References specific SLS section numbers or requirements
criteria_results.reasoning: Findings cite specific SLS sections (§3.1, §4.3, §6.1, §9.1, etc.).

criteria_results.title: Identifies SLS requirements with no corresponding Agreement provision
criteria_results.reasoning: Part V lists requirements on which the Agreement is silent, e.g., HITRUST, pen testing, TAP, data breach termination.

criteria_results.title: Notes interconnection between maintenance exclusions and uptime gap
criteria_results.reasoning: A-4 and Appendix A.1 combine maintenance exclusions with 99.5% to show ~94.1% effective availability; Executive Summary notes maintenance makes the gap worse.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Meridian as the client and Cloudvance as the vendor
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo consistently treats Meridian as customer/client and Cloudvance as vendor.

criteria_results.title: Notes SLS requirement for 72-hour advance notice of scheduled maintenance
criteria_results.reasoning: A-4 and key metrics table note SLS 72 hours' notice vs Agreement 24 hours and Sat/Sun 12-6 AM window.

criteria_results.title: Identifies SLS requirement for service credits refundable in cash
criteria_results.reasoning: B-2 notes SLS invoice credit or cash refund at Meridian's election vs Agreement 'not redeemable for cash'.

criteria_results.title: Notes audit cost allocation gap (Meridian's expense vs. vendor's expense)
criteria_results.reasoning: H-1 notes Agreement audits at Customer's sole expense vs SLS vendor reimbursement on material non-compliance.
